evidence.source_sentence: The $M _ { \mathrm { n } }$of the obtained poly(MPC) brushes on the silicon wafer were estimated to be approximately 30,000  120,000 by SEC of the corresponding free polymer using water as the eluent.

The AFM observation revealed that a homogeneous polymer layer was formed on the substrate, and the surface roughness was $0 . 8 \sim 1 . 5$nm in the dried state in a $5 \times 5 \mu \mathrm { m } ^ { 2 }$scanning area.
The thickness of the poly(MPC) brush was determined to be ca. 10  40 nm by ellipsometry.
The graft density was estimated to be ca. 0.22 $\mathrm { c h a i n s } / \mathrm { n m } ^ { 2 }$based on the linear relationship between $M _ { \mathrm { n } }$and the thickness.
Similarly, the graft density of the poly(DMAEMA) brush was determined to be 0.40 chains/nm<sup>2</sup>.
Advancing and receding contact angles of poly(MPC) brushes against water were $1 1 ^ { \circ }$and $5 \sim 7 ^ { \circ }$, respectively.

The scattering length density profiles of the poly(MPC) brushes in $\mathbf { D } _ { 2 } \mathbf { O }$calculated from the reflectivity curves indicated that the poly(METAI) chains were stretched up to 60 nm in $\mathbf { D } _ { 2 } \mathbf { O } _ { 3 }$, forming a concentration gradient of ${ \bf D } _ { 2 } { \bf O } .$.

For instance, assuming the swollen brush thickness was 60 nm, the $M _ { \mathrm { n } }$was 126,000, and grafting density was 0.40 chains/nm<sup>2</sup>, the ionic concentration in swollen poly (METAI) brush layer can be estimated to be 4.2 M, which is much higher than salt concentration in aqueous solution.
